title: Neon Blast
premise: A neon-styled arcade space shooter where the player pilots a glowing starfighter, auto-fires upward, and survives by dodging and destroying falling meteor-like enemies.
interaction_model: Mouse or touch controls horizontal ship movement only; shooting is automatic; the game runs in real time on a fullscreen canvas with quick restart loops.
objective: Survive as long as possible, destroy incoming enemies, and earn the highest score before colliding with a falling threat.
progression: Single-run score chasing with no meta-upgrades; difficulty increases during the run through faster enemy pressure and denser pacing.
mood: Arcade, energetic, glowing, futuristic, lightweight, replay-driven
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual browser arcade games, simple controls, and quick score-attack sessions on desktop or mobile.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a casual space shooter with automatic firing and horizontal dodge control.
High confidence that the primary enemies are intended as meteors or hostile falling space objects, based on the subtitle and descending obstacle behavior.
Moderate confidence on narrative framing, since the theme is mostly conveyed through UI text and visual style rather than explicit story systems.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser-based neon arcade space shooter called Neon Blast. Present it as a fullscreen canvas game with a glowing sci-fi HUD, a title/start panel, a game-over panel, and a quick restart flow. The player controls a small starfighter positioned near the bottom of the screen and can only move it horizontally using mouse movement on desktop and touch drag on mobile. The ship should fire automatically upward at a steady rhythm, so the player’s main skill is lining up shots while dodging danger. Spawn colorful meteor-like or hostile diamond-shaped space objects from random positions above the screen and make them fall downward at varying speeds and sizes. When bullets hit enemies, destroy them instantly, create bright particle explosions, play punchy sound effects, flash a reactive hit visual, and add to the score. If any enemy collides with the player ship, end the run immediately, stop the background music, play a failure cue, show the final score, and allow an instant reboot/restart. Make the background feel alive with animated stars, subtle nebula gradients, glowing streaks, and strong cyan-pink-gold neon highlights. Keep the progression simple and arcade-like: no inventory, no upgrades, no levels beyond an endless run, just rising intensity as score increases through faster or more frequent enemy spawns. The overall tone should be flashy, accessible, responsive on mobile, and built around fast replayable score-chasing sessions.
